Does it do the right thing?

Six panels, each one live. Drive them with the buttons, or press Run to watch a scripted sequence play out slowly and end in a verdict. Real React, real roots, no test harness and no act() — this is the browser’s own scheduler.

Rebasing, in the order you can see

A sync action applies to the state on screen, not to the state a held transition is waiting on. When the transition commits, the actions are re-ordered into the order they were dispatched — the screen goes from bc to Abc without ever showing a state nobody asked for, and without the fallback ever appearing.

Nobody arrives early

A reader revealed while a transition is blocked — by a sibling appearing, or by an Activity tree being shown — displays what the rest of the page displays. It waits for the tree to commit rather than starting a transition of its own and arriving first. Readings come from layout effects and ref callbacks, never from the DOM.

Suspense: the fallback you asked for, and the one you did not

A sync update to a pending promise shows the fallback. The same update inside a transition keeps the current content and waits. That second half is what useSyncExternalStore gives up: it de-opts the transition to sync and drops to the fallback regardless. The fallback is counted by DOM attach, not by render.

An error boundary that can actually be reset

use() throws the same rejection every time it reads it, so resetting a boundary on its own puts you straight back in the fallback — watch the catch count go up. The store's current promise is the reset key, so moving the store on is what clears it.

Selectors skip the render, without an equality function

A slice nobody selected moves nothing. A selector that returns its previous result when the slice is equivalent keeps both the render and the object identity stable. Renders are counted on commit, so a render React discarded is not counted against it.

Two roots, one store, no provider

Separate createRoot trees share a store and stay in step, including while one is blocked on a transition and the other is not, and with StrictMode double-rendering only one of them.
